To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) crowdsourcing techniques can be effectively used to solve a range ontology engineering problems, (2) crowdsourcing can be integrated closely into ontology engineering work, (3) the uComp Protegé plugin facilitates such an integration and (4) its use reduces the workload of ontology engineers and leads to data of similar or better quality.

crowdsourcing tasks that are recurrently used in ontology engineering can be effectively integrated into ontology engineering work, and that this integration can be facilitated with a tool that is closely integrated into ontology engineering environments.

the uComp plugin facilitates the integration of crowdsourcing tasks into the work of the ontology engineers and that this integration reduces the time needed for ontology engineering tasks by a factor of 11 and leads to data of comparable quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to best integrate crowdsourcing into the ontology engineering work of ontology engineers.
the integration of crowdsourcing into the ontology engineering work of ontology engineers and shows that such integration is effective in terms of time, costs and quality.

the development of a tool that enables ontology engineers to easily use crowdsourcing to improve the quality of their ontologies, and to do so in a way that minimizes their working times and task costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uComp Protegé plugin can be used to successfully integrate crowdsourcing into the ontology engineering process.
crowdsourcing is a very effective means to solve ontology engineering tasks.

the uComp plugin facilitates ontology engineering by providing an easy to use and flexible crowdsourcing interface that allows ontology engineers to efficiently and effectively use crowd workers for a variety of ontology related tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

crowdsourcing techniques can be used to solve a variety of ontology problems, that crowdsourcing techniques are not limited to a single type of ontology problem, that crowdsourcing tasks can be integrated into ontology engineering work, and that crowdsourcing techniques lead to significant cost savings in the ontology engineering process.
the integration of crowdsourcing tasks into the ontology engineering process, can lead to substantial improvements in terms of cost, time, and quality of the ontology engineering process.
we show how to closely integrate typical crowdsourcing tasks for solving a range of ontology tasks into the ontology engineering work of ontology engineers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crowdsourcing can be effectively integrated into ontology engineering work.
the integration of crowdsourcing into ontology editing environments can be a powerful means of improving the quality and efficiency of ontology engineering.
crowdsourcing can be effectively integrated into ontology engineering, leading to a more cost effective and efficient way to create and maintain ontologies.
